title: Al-Mu'min, the Giver of Safety
hook: the Giver of Safety and faith

segments.voice: Yesterday, As-Salam, Peace itself, the name inside the greeting. Your line was peace is his name. Who did you greet slowly, meaning every word? Day two hundred forty-one.

Think of the person you'd call at three in the morning. Not the funniest friend or the smartest one. The safe one. The one who wouldn't tell anyone, wouldn't make you feel stupid, would just pick up. Most of us can count those people on one hand. Long before the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ received any revelation, the people of Mecca had a nickname for him. They left their valuables with him when they traveled. They called him al-Amin, the trustworthy one, the safe one. Today's name comes from the same three letters, and it's a word you already know as the word for a believer. Today: Al-Mu'min, the Giver of Safety.
screen: `THE ONE YOU'D CALL AT 3AM.` → `AL-AMIN, THE TRUSTWORTHY.` → `THE SAME THREE LETTERS.`

segments.voice: The root is a-m-n. It grows a whole family. Amn: safety, the absence of fear. Amanah: a trust, something left in your keeping. Iman: faith. Amin: trustworthy. And the word Muslims say after the Fatiha, amin, so be it. At the end of al-Hashr, after Peace, comes al-Mu'min. Pickthall translates it the Keeper of Faith, and scholars give the name two meanings that sit together. First, the one who grants safety. The Qur'an says in Surah Quraysh that the Lord of the House fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear. Safety from fear is His gift. Second, the one who confirms: who affirms the truth of His messengers and keeps faith with His promises. He never breaks trust. Now the surprise. Mu'min is also the everyday word for a believer, a person of faith. The same word names Allah and names the people who trust Him. And the Prophet tied the two together in a way that's very practical. Tirmidhi and Nasa'i record him saying: the mu'min is the one from whom people's lives and property are safe. The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe, says another hadith in Bukhari. So a believer, in this sense, isn't first someone who holds the right ideas. It's someone people feel safe around. The name tells you what the one you trust is like, and what the one who trusts is meant to become.
screen: `A-M-N — SAFETY, TRUST, FAITH, AMIN.` · `THE ONE WHO GRANTS SAFETY.` · `THE ONE WHO CONFIRMS AND KEEPS FAITH.` · `A BELIEVER PEOPLE FEEL SAFE AROUND.` · then, large: `THE ONE WHO MAKES SAFE.`

segments.voice: Sit, and remember a time you felt completely safe with someone. Where were you? What did they do, or not do? Let the feeling come back into your body: the shoulders dropping, the breath getting longer. Stay there for a few breaths. Then think of one person in your life who might not feel safe right now, at home, at work, in their own head. What would make them feel even a little safer around you? A kept secret. A calm voice. Showing up when you said you would. The bell holds the time.
Al-Mu'min. The Giver of Safety, who grants safety from fear and keeps faith; also the word for a believer. Today's word.
Your line: the one who makes safe. Today, do the one thing that would make that person feel safer around you, and keep one thing someone told you in confidence. Day two hundred forty-one.

howItsDone: Muslims describe the believer, the mu'min, by how safe others are around them, and treat promises, secrets and anything left in their care as an amanah, a trust; al-Amin, the trustworthy, was the Prophet's nickname in Mecca.

the one from whom people's lives and property are safe

fork.reveal: the mu'min is the one people are safe with, in their lives and property (Tirmidhi; Nasa'i).

original.note: Arabic: the Giver of Safety, the Keeper of Faith; also, a believer. from a-m-n.

trapdoor: what you thought: al-Mu'min means God believes.
what it means: the one who grants safety from fear and keeps faith, and the word for a believer too.
what a scholar hears: a-m-n gives amn, amanah, iman and amin; 59:23, the Keeper of Faith; Tirmidhi 2627, people safe from the mu'min.

sources.ref: Qur'an 106:3–4 (who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2627; Sunan an-Nasa'i 4995 (the mu'min is the one people's lives and property are safe from)
Sahih al-Bukhari 10 (the Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe)
Ibn Hisham, Sirah (al-Amin, the Meccans' name for Muhammad)
